title: fix(drilling): include drill point length in through holes, stock sim, and MCP
body:
## What changed

- Added `BreakThroughFrom` (`FullDiameter` by default, or `Tip`) to `Drill` parameters, UI (`Break-through from` combo in `holes_page.rs`), MCP DTOs, and project v68 (`PROJECT_VERSION = 68`).
- Added `drill_point_length` and `through_tip_run` in `camcraft_motion::drilling`. In `FullDiameter` mode on twist drills outside `Spot`, `Tap`, `FloatingTap`, and `Ream`, `through_tip_run` adds `(diameter / 2) / tan(tip_angle / 2)` (`180 deg -> 0.0`). Non-finite or out-of-range tip angles fail by name. Lathe axial drills keep `Tip` mode for `axial_doors` clearance.
- Migrated pre-v68 projects without `break_through_from` to `Tip` in `settle_drill_break_through`. Existing saved files keep their cached depths and posted Z.
- Added `SdfTool::Drill` and `RevKind::Drill` (`drill_dist`) in `camcraft_sim::stock_sim`, plus `simulate_drill` and `simulate_drill_display` across plain, display, carried, held, playback, field-view, and rest simulation.
- Listed `break_through` (`number`, default `null`) on `drill`, `bore`, and `thread` in `list_operation_types` (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`).

## Cause

Through holes with a twist drill added only `break_through` (`1.0 mm` default) to the tip depth, stopping the cylindrical margin ~0.803 mm short on a Ø6 118° drill. Both column and field stock simulation also modeled drills as flat cylinders at full diameter, hiding the uncut cone lip. Separately, `kind_defaults()` skipped `None` fields on serialization, so `list_operation_types` omitted `break_through`.

## Tests

### Pins (red before fix, green after)
- `issue_2441_through_hole_drill_adds_point_length_and_posts_full_breakthrough` (`crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`): failed before fix (`deepest tip must include the 118 deg drill point (-2.803), got -1.000`), passes after fix (posts `Z-19.803` and clears both sims at `r=2.5`).
- `issue_2441_stock_sim_models_drill_point_cone_lip_when_stopped_at_floor` (`crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`): failed before fix (`got z=0.000` flat bottom), passes after fix (leaves `~1.5 mm` cone lip at `r=2.5` in both sims when tip stops at `z=0`).
- `issue_2441_mcp_list_operation_types_lists_break_through` (`crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`): failed before fix (`drill is missing break_through`), passes after fix for `drill`, `bore`, `thread`, and `break_through_from`.
- `issue_2441_mcp_can_patch_break_through_and_break_through_from`, `drill_point_length_respects_tip_angle_and_refuses_bad_angles`, `through_exit_clears_the_floor`, `drill_engines_cut_cone_with_cylindrical_flute_and_agree`, `drill_break_through_from_defaults_to_full_diameter_and_switches_to_tip`: all pass.

### Mutation checks
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs` (`through_tip_run` reverted to `p.through_clear`): `issue_2441_through_hole_drill_adds_point_length_and_posts_full_breakthrough` failed RED -> restored GREEN.
- `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (`ToolKind::Drill` cone & `drill` flag reverted to `(None, false)`): `issue_2441_stock_sim_models_drill_point_cone_lip_when_stopped_at_floor` failed RED -> restored GREEN.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs` (`break_through` injection removed in `list_operation_types`): `issue_2441_mcp_list_operation_types_lists_break_through` failed RED -> restored GREEN.
- `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` (`settle_drill_break_through` skipped for `from < 68`): `v65_preserves_cutting_steps_and_loads_v63_break_through_and_v62_defaults` failed RED -> restored GREEN.

### Gate and Clippy
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (`exit 0`).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (at `5485b6476`): 589/592 steps passed in 78.2 minutes. All `sim` (41/41), `motion` (5/5), and `ui` (9/9) steps passed. Three `camcraft-app` suites reported failures:
  - `shoulder_adaptive` (`containment_outside_clears_past_the_edge_never_the_recess` hit its 60 s debug timer under 6-way contention, tracked by #2453): re-running `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test shoulder_adaptive -- --test-threads=1` passed 9/9 (69.42s).
  - `microarc_test_part` (`a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, `3246 != 3245` lines): pre-existing failure on `upstream/main` tracked by #2483 and reproduced in `upstream/main` post-merge CI run `44279917425`.
  - `stock_source_holes` (`framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number`): pre-existing failure on `upstream/main` since `7bcc13a4b` and reproduced in `upstream/main` post-merge CI run `44279917425`.
- Targeted suites observed inside the `5485b6476` gate run: `break_through` (12/12), `operations` (120/120, 6 ignored), `first_router_part` (4/4), `example_catalog` (2/2), `mcp` (22/22), `golden_cl` (33/33), `solid_law_goldens` (7/7).

## Goldens moved

- No `.cl` goldens changed (`git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.cl"` is empty).
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` (plus `first-part.camproj` and `README.md`): only the four `Drill1` (`DR-0600`) cycles moved (`G73 X... Y... Z-1. R22. Q18. F300` -> `G83 X... Y... Z-2.803 R22. Q6. F300`), as adding the `1.803 mm` point crosses the `4d` (`24 mm`) `Auto` depth threshold into `G83`.
- `examples/first-router-part.camproj` (plus `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-router-part.md`): regenerated `Drill1` moves and cycle `bottom_z` from `-1.0` to `-2.802582` (`G73 ... Z-14.803` in `G54`); `2D Pocket1` and `2D Contour1` paths are unchanged.

## Not exercised

- Interactive GPU viewport rendering was not run; field and column drill cones were checked numerically in unit tests and `stock_view::field_view`.
- Radial cross drilling (`cross_drill`) keeps its own existing through math and does not read `break_through_from`.
- The full `release` tier (with `--ignored` heavy lanes and Windows UI pixel snapshots) was not run.

## Overlaps

Touches the same file (different functions/arms or regenerated assets; whichever merges second refreshes):
- #2503 (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` 2D extension / keep-law arm)
- #2488 (`crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` `freeze_legacy_tool_numbers`, `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` `ToolDto`)
- #2486 (`examples/first-router-part.camproj`)

- #2253 (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, `generate.rs`, `project/file.rs` `PROJECT_VERSION`, `project/apply.rs`, `crates/app/tests/units_in_refusals.rs`; already has `conflicts`)
- #2149 (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, `generate.rs`, `project/file.rs`, `project/apply.rs`; already has `conflicts`)
- #2134 (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, `project/file.rs`, `project/apply.rs`, `crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`; already has `conflicts`)
- #2092 (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs`, `project/apply.rs`, `crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`)
- #2024 (`crates/app/src/project/apply.rs`)
- #1713 (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` Finish3D arms, `kinds.rs`, `project/params.rs`, `project/params_impl.rs`, `crates/app/tests/golden_cl.rs`, `crates/app/tests/operations.rs`, `crates/motion/tests/center_cut_owed.rs`)

title: fix(2d): keep extension out of islands and note uncut corners
body:
## What changed

- Populated `AreaCtx::blocked` in `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_ctx.rs` for whole-model (`SrcRef::Entity`) and stock-source (`SrcRef::Stock`) pocket-family operations (`2D Pocket`, `2D Adaptive`, `2D Offset`) while keeping `islands` as `false`.
- Added `unreached_corners` and `unreached_corner_note` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` (re-exported in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`) to detect residual sharp-corner cusps wider than `0.03 mm` half-width and clip them against the setup stock outline so extended air corners do not warn.
- Updated `keep_law::narrow_noted` and its call site in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` to append the corner residual note on clearing operations around parts.
- Surfaced non-empty operation `path.notes` as `"notes"` in `crates/app/src/script/api.rs::op_view` so MCP `generate` and `verify` report the corner note without changing empty responses.
- Updated `crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs` (`a_whole_model_extension_keeps_the_part_and_posts`), added `crates/app/tests/adaptive_zero_margin_island.rs`, and recorded the choices in `docs/decisions/2438-adaptive-zero-margin-corners.md`.

## Cause

Default whole-model and stock-source clearing keeps the cutter inside the setup stock box, which necessarily leaves uncut triangular corner cusps at sharp 90-degree stock corners around an island. The narrow-band detector only reported whole disconnected bands that eroded to empty, and `op_view` did not expose `path.notes`, so callers saw an `ok` verdict with silent unreached stock corners. Meanwhile, `boundary_ctx::build` left `blocked = None` for `SrcRef::Entity` and `SrcRef::Stock` pocket-family operations, so setting `Boundary` `extension` to clear the stock corners shrank the interior island hole too and drove cuts straight through standing part geometry.

## Tests

- **Pins (`crates/app/tests/adaptive_zero_margin_island.rs`)**:
  - `zero_margin_adaptive_around_island_names_uncut_stock_corners`: failed on unchanged `7bcc13a4b` (missing `notes` in MCP `generate`), passes after fix (verifies `rest.max > 4.0` and corner note on `generate` and `verify`).
  - `extension_on_island_on_plate_grows_only_exterior_clears_corners_part_source` and `_stock_source`: failed on unchanged `7bcc13a4b` (`verify` reported island gouges), pass after fix (zero gouge cells, stock corners cleared to floor, posts cleanly, no corner note).
  - `extension_with_top_allowance_keeps_island_untouched_and_clears_corners`: failed on unchanged `7bcc13a4b` (`Gouge` + `RapidInStock`), passes after fix under `+2 mm` stock allowance.
- **Unit tests (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs::law`)**: 4 tests pass (`sharp_stock_corners_around_island_are_named_until_extended`, `filleted_corners_and_unreached_bands_emit_no_corner_note`, `a_band_narrower_than_the_tool_beside_a_wide_bore_is_named`, `a_noise_sliver_and_an_empty_region_say_nothing`).
- **Keep law (`crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs`)**: `a_whole_model_extension_keeps_the_part_and_posts` passes while `a_whole_model_area_offset_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts` and `stock_source` keep pins stay intact.
- **Mutation checks**:
  - Reverted `boundary_ctx.rs` to `upstream/main`: `extension_*` pins in `adaptive_zero_margin_island` failed (3 failed); restored: passed.
  - Reverted `keep_law.rs` + `generate.rs` to `upstream/main`: `zero_margin_adaptive_around_island_names_uncut_stock_corners` failed (`generate notes missing corner warning`); restored: passed.
  - Reverted `script/api.rs` to `upstream/main`: `zero_margin_adaptive_around_island_names_uncut_stock_corners` failed (`generate exposes op notes`); restored: passed.
- **Clippy & Gate**:
  - `cargo xtask gate batch --only clippy` (`--all-targets -- -D warnings` across all workspace crates): passed in 366s.
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 200 of 202 steps passed (all `motion` suites + 140 of 142 `app` suites, including `adaptive_zero_margin_island` in 39s, `keep_law`, `narrow_band`, `adaptive_pinch`, `area_controls`, `area_overhead`, `setup_align_2d_area`, `mcp_verify`, `mcp_generate`).
  - `app:shoulder_adaptive::containment_outside_clears_past_the_edge_never_the_recess` failed its 60s timer under parallel gate load (81.90s) and passed when run alone (`47.97s`).
  - `app:stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` failed on a pre-existing `chamfer_ride::ride_loops` error (`has no wall under it`); re-running on unmodified branch base `7bcc13a4b` (`#2450`) produced the exact same failure in 0.01s.

## Goldens moved

None (`git diff --stat upstream/main` / `7bcc13a4b` on `*.nc` and `*.cl` is empty).

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate release` (heavy `#[ignore]` lanes and UI snapshots; no UI code changed).
- Pre-existing failing test `stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` remains red from `#2450` on `upstream/main`.

## Overlaps

- `#2149` touches `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_ctx.rs` (`part_solid_of`, `area_ctx`, `op_stamp`) and `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (`Pocket`/`Offset2D`/`Pocket3D`), different functions/lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2253` touches `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (`Pocket`) and `crates/app/src/script/api.rs::op_view` (inside `if warnings`), different block/lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2460` and `#1713` touch `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (`Contour` and `Finish3D` arms), different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2487` (merged to `upstream/main` after `7bcc13a4b`) touches `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs` line 124 (`contour_run_side`), different line from our line 142 (`unreached`).

Changelog: Whole-model and stock-source 2D clearing now reports unreached stock corners in notes (and MCP generate/verify) and keeps standing part islands blocked when extending outside the stock.
Fixes #2438

title: feat(post): carry a flipped WCS X or Y into the posted program
body:
## Why

The maintainer wrote (2026-11-17): "WCS54, X flipped - posting and generating are refused until the flip is cleared..  the ability to flip axis from a positive to negative is fundamental and should not be blocked.. posting and generation should take it into consideration rather.."

## What changed

- Generation, verification and the stock simulation no longer refuse a flipped setup. They stay in the setup frame, so the cut does not change.
- The job writes `PARAM WcsFlip` on each section of a flipped setup. A new post pass (`crates/post/src/post/wcs_flip.rs`) runs before `wcs_rotate` and `invert`. It mirrors the flipped axis about the work origin through `invert::translate_rules`.
- One flipped axis swaps G2/G3 and G41/G42. Two flipped axes (X and Y) keep them. Helix, canned cycles and probing (with `probeAxisInversion`) are carried.
- The flip composes with a machine-inverted axis.
- The travel check, the setup sheet and the viewport work envelope read the posted sign.
- `fanuc.cps` and `haas.cps` state `axisInversion = true` and name the flipped axes in the program header.
- The MCP flip tool and `get_job` report the refusal only for the cases that still refuse.

## Cases

Carried: Flip X, Flip Y, and Flip X+Y on 3-axis mill sections, with Fanuc and Haas.

Refused by name, with the flip as the cause:

- a flipped Z (follow-up #2474)
- a script without `axisInversion = true` (follow-up #2475)
- a flip together with a WCS rotation (follow-up #2476)
- turning, threading, live tool, ABC/tilt, EDM, wire and plasma sections
- a section that uses a modal origin or start across a change of flip
- a `WcsFlip` value that the pass cannot read

The decision file `docs/decisions/1649-wcs-flip-carry.md` has the case table and the reasons.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs` (13 tests), for example `a_flipped_wcs_cuts_the_cam_path`, `one_flipped_axis_reverses_arcs_and_the_compensation_side_and_two_do_not`, `a_flipped_axis_on_an_inverted_machine_axis_posts_the_standard_signs`, `a_flipped_z_refuses_by_name`, `a_flipped_and_rotated_section_refuses_by_name`, `a_section_that_leans_on_a_modal_origin_across_a_flip_change_refuses`
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_flip_post.rs` (8 tests), for example `a_flipped_x_or_y_posts_the_mirrored_program_and_clearing_it_posts_as_before`, `generation_runs_in_a_flipped_setup_and_the_toolpath_does_not_change`, `the_travel_check_reads_the_posted_sign_of_a_flipped_axis`, `the_work_envelope_mirrors_about_the_origin_on_a_flipped_axis`
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_flip.rs` (7 tests), with `the_mcp_tool_sets_the_flags_and_get_job_shows_them`
- `crates/ui` `wcs_flip_tests`

## Gate

Quick gate (`gate-logs/quick-20261118-074008`): 858 steps, 857 ok. The one red step is clippy on `crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs:128` (`.map(&resolve)`). That lint is on main before this branch and is tracked by #2479. This branch does not touch that file. Clippy of the touched crates with that one lint allowed is clean. `git merge-tree` with `origin/main` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The other post scripts (they refuse until #2475 verifies them).
- A real controller.
- Lathe and multi-axis programs (they refuse by name).

## Labels and notes

Effort: max. The issue did not escalate.

Process change: yes (one row in the `camcraft-mcp` skill).

Changelog: A setup's Flip X / Flip Y no longer refuses generation and the post: Fanuc and Haas programs mirror the flipped axis, with the arc direction and compensation side kept correct. A flipped Z and the other post scripts still refuse by name.

Fixes #1649

title: fix(post): refuse a Tormach move with no A word in an indexed operation
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/tormach.cps` (`indexFor`): a rapid or linear record with no A word is refused by name when the operation holds an A that is not 0 (modulo 360). The post does not write the refused move.
- Before this change, the post read the record as tool angle 0. Since #2386 it then wrote a `G0` / `G1` block with an `A0` word in the middle of the operation. That turn swings the part under the tool.
- A record with no A word in an upright operation posts as before. A record with no A word after a stated `A0` posts as before.
- Refusal text: `move in operation <name> states no A angle while the operation holds A<angle> - the post turns A inside an operation only on a move that states its A angle`.

## Readings

- Reproduced: on the main post script, the two refusal tests fail (no warning, the move posts). With the fix, they pass.
- Source reading of the stream: `post::dump` (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs`, the `(None, None)` arm) gives a record with no angle when the CL move states no axis. Its comment says that such a move "keeps the modal pose". A real turn back to upright gets an explicit `A0` (the `(None, Some(_)) if tilted` arm). Thus a record with no A word after a non-zero A is never a stated turn.
- No generator was found that emits such a record: the CL path attaches the modal axis to each move. The refusal is a guard. It refuses no known legal program.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2473-tormach-a-without-word.md` (refuse, not keep the section angle, and why).

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/tormach_no_a_word.rs`:
- `a_rapid_with_no_a_word_in_an_indexed_operation_is_refused`
- `a_linear_move_with_no_a_word_in_an_indexed_operation_is_refused`
- `a_stated_turn_to_a0_then_a_move_with_no_a_word_still_posts`

## Gate (local, Windows, debug, -j 6)

The quick gate selects all 862 steps for a post script change. For that reason I ran the binaries that load `tormach.cps`, one step for each binary:

- `camcraft-post --tests`: all binaries pass (88 test results ok).
- `camcraft-app`: pass for `conformance`, `first_4axis_part`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`, `mcp_rotary_stack`, `post_spindle_rule_all`, `program_units`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `rotary_subplate`, `rotary_subplate_standing`, `setup_mount`, `tilt_a180`, `tormach_end_units`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `tormach_post`, `tormach_program_end`, `tormach_safe_retract`, `tormach_toolchange_lift`, `tormach_wrapped_a`, `wcs_index`, `wcs_rotation_control`.
- `camcraft-app microarc_test_part`: `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` fails. This is the known main failure #2483. It fails with the same text on the main post script (`wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc: line count 3246 != 3245`). The new refusal text does not occur in its output.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass.

## Not exercised

- No recorded `.cl` from a real operation that emits such a record. No generator was found that does.
- The other `camcraft-app` suites that load Tormach machines (lathe, plasma, probe) were not run. They do not use the A rotary path of `indexFor`.
- Not run on a PathPilot control.
- No pixel snapshot changed.

Effort: high (not escalated).

- `AddTool::new` assigns the lowest unused controller number in `1-99999` (`tool_numbers::next_free`), stores it on `ToolDef::number`, and exposes `AddTool::number()`.

- `project::apply::check_and_apply` freezes legacy unnumbered `EntityKind::Tool` records to their 1-based name-sorted list position on load without emitting load notes.
- `SetToolNumber::new` refuses `None` by tool name so tools always keep an explicit number, while permitting the same number across disjoint setup machines (`setup_mount::machine_of`).

title: fix(2d): join open contour runs and handle inside corners
body:
## What changed

- Added `camcraft_geometry::boundary_chains::join_open_runs` to deduplicate XY-coincident open runs regardless of direction and weld touching runs end to end. Single-point and non-finite runs pass through unchanged so operation generation refuses them by name.
- Called `join_open_runs` on `chains` in `selection_geometry_impl` (`crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs`) for `OpParams::Contour`, `OpParams::PlasmaProfile`, and `OpParams::WireContour`.
- Added `pub fn offset_run_side` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_run_side.rs` and re-exported it in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`. Both `contour_run_side::offset_run` and `crates/app/src/operation/contour_open.rs` (`offset_run`) now call it.
- Filtered `Region::sweep` loops to one outer CCW loop so inner CW holes from bridged bottleneck notches do not abort the offset.
- Added `corner_sector_left` for acute convex join arcs wrapping past 90 deg, `CAP_TIE` (`0.006 mm`) for arc-sag tie-breaking, and `nearest_on_run` clearance checks before inserting perpendicular `normal_at` endpoints on short inside-corner legs.
- Added decision record `docs/decisions/2277-contour-inside-corners.md`.

## Cause

- `stitch_open_runs` only closes full rings into `loops`, so manually picked open contour edges remained separate runs. Offsetting each run on its own drove the tool across inside corners into adjacent walls (`Z 0.000 near (40.000, 10.995)` on the U-notched block).
- On connected open chains, `offset_run` rejected inner CW holes across bridged bottleneck notches, misclassified acute convex join arcs with `cross`, added swallowed `normal_at` endpoints on short legs, and lost end-cap intersections within Clipper2's `5 um` arc sag.

- Reverting `offset_run` in `crates/app/src/operation/contour_open.rs`: 1 pin failed in `contour_open_side`; restoring passed 6/6.

title: fix(motion): 2D Contour tab width is the bridge that stays, not the centre-path gap
body:
## What changed

2D Contour tabs now leave a bridge of the tab width that the user sets.

- `ring::tab_window` (new): the tab window on the tool-centre ring is `tab_width + tool_diameter`. Before, it was `tab_width` alone. The cutter disc removes `D/2` more material past each window end, so the bridge on the channel centre line was `tab_width - D`. A tab width of `D` or less left no bridge, and the part came free with no message.
- `ring::tabs_fill_note` (new): when the tab windows fill the whole loop, the tabbed level cuts nothing. The operation notes now say this. Before, this was silent.
- `contour.rs` calls the two helpers (3 lines more in a file that was over the 400-line target before this PR).

## Readings

- Square 40 x 40, 6 mm cutter, outside contour, bottom level tabbed:
  - 4 tabs of 6 mm: four bridges of 6.0 mm (before: none).
  - 4 tabs of 5 mm: four bridges of 5.0 mm (before: none, the cuts overlapped by 1 mm).
  - 3 tabs of 10 mm: three bridges of 10.0 mm (before: 4 mm).
- `tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor`: the tabbed level is `4 x (6 + 10) = 64` mm shorter than the full ring (measured 64.0017 mm; the 1.7 um comes from window ends that fall on corner arcs).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/tests/contour_tabs.rs` (new): measures each bridge as the swept disc of the posted feeds against points on the tool-centre ring. Five tests, including the fill note.
- `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs`:
  - `tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor`: new length.
  - `contour_tabs_stand_down_the_entry_arms` and `contour_hop_rides_the_tall_tab_top`: these used four 6 mm tabs with a 10 mm tool on a 40 mm centre ring. No tab can stand there. They now use two 4 mm tabs; their asserts did not change.
- `crates/app/tests/first_router_part.rs`: `examples/first-router-part.camproj` regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. Its contour now has 14 mm gaps on the centre path for the 8 mm tabs with the 6 mm cutter. The write also took the project file from version 62 to 67 and added the drill's break-through note.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick` on the final code: 22 steps, 0 failed (motion lib and the touched motion suites, app `arc_entry`, `solid_law_goldens`, `wall_arc_entry`). Then `first_router_part`: 4 passed after the regenerate. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine.
- Control compensation (G41/G42) rings use the same window; on a straight wall the bridge is the same. Not measured separately.
- Wire EDM tabs (`wire_edm/tabs.rs`) are a different law and are not changed.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md`.

Changelog: 2D Contour: the tab width is now the width of the bridge that stays on the part (the tab window on the tool path is the tab width plus the tool diameter). Before, a tab width equal to or less than the tool diameter left no tab, and the part came free.

Fixes #2480

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster_bridge.rs` (new): `bridge_line` joins two pieces of one raster line with one straight feed. All three of these conditions must be true:
  1. The XY gap is not wider than the tool diameter (`2r`).
  2. The slope is not steeper than 45 degrees (`SPLIT_MZ`) plus the tolerance.
  3. The swept ball stays `r - eps_chord` clear of each facet. The check uses `stock_sim::dist_seg_tri`, as `column_clear` does.
- `raster_pass_spaced` calls `bridge_line` on each line before the serpentine reverse. Parallel, ParallelMulti, Scallop, blend and swarf share this code path.
- A hole that the ball fits into keeps its hop to the safe height. The pin in `finish3d_land` for the 3.4 mm bolt holes stays green.
- `swarf`, `swarf_multi` and `norm_dir` move from `raster.rs` to `swarf.rs`, with no change of behaviour. `raster.rs` was 411 lines and is now 305 lines.
- `docs/decisions/2431-parallel-over-holes.md` records the decisions.

## Readings

- Root cause: `support_at` gives only facet tangency and convex folds between shallow facets. A hole rim is a shallow-to-steep edge, so the march has no support over the hole. Each line then hopped, also over holes smaller than the ball. A lid step a hair off the rim gives the same gap (a `sqrt(2 r dz)` stretch).
- With the bridge removed, `a_hole_narrower_than_the_ball_is_crossed_without_a_pick` and `an_open_slot_narrower_than_the_ball_is_crossed_without_a_pick` fail. With the bridge, they pass.
- The other three tests are guards. They pass with and without the bridge: the 0.01 mm lid step is already crossed on main, the wide hole keeps its hop, and a 1 mm shelf edge is not bridged.
- Each test samples each straight feed at 0.05 mm against the real model. The deepest bite is not more than the tolerance.

## Pinning tests

`crates/motion/tests/finish3d_holes.rs`:
- `a_hole_narrower_than_the_ball_is_crossed_without_a_pick`

title: perf(xtask): run release-gate suites in a longest-first queue; narrow the alone list
body:
Process change: yes

For the maintainer's decision - a process change (xtask). Measured before/after on the same Hetzner ccx43 (16 cores): numbers follow in a comment.

## Why

On a 16-core server the release gate used every core for the ~10 min of builds, then ~80% of the run used one or two cores. Three causes in `xtask/src`: `lanes::alone()` sent every camcraft-app / camcraft-kernel step to run alone, one after another; `lanes::waves` grouped the other steps into barrier waves that each waited for their slowest lane; and the alone steps used the default budget of 6.

## What changed

- **A. A narrower alone list** (`lanes.rs`). Builds (`--no-run`), clippy, every UI step (`in_ui` or camcraft-ui) and an app/kernel step that is not one named target still run alone. Of the single app/kernel targets, only `lanes::ISOLATED` runs alone. Every other app/kernel target now joins the shared lanes.
- **B. A work queue in place of barrier waves** (new `queue.rs`). The builds run first, each alone. Then `budget::lane_limit` lanes of `budget::per_lane` jobs each pull the next step as they finish. The alone steps run last, one at a time, with the whole budget. The queue runs the longest steps first (Graham's LPT rule), using the per-step seconds the previous release run wrote to `gate-logs/release-*/timings.tsv`. Every release run now writes that file. A step with no recorded time ranks with the longest, and with no history at all the queue keeps plan order.
- The checkout guard (VOID) now runs before every queued step. A failed build still stops the run, and a failed suite still stops nothing.
- **C. Alone steps use the whole budget for `--test-threads`.** This already happens through `budget::scale` (the plan's `6` is the default budget). The gate now prints a note when the machine has more cores than the budget, because `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16` is what lets a 16-core runner use all its cores. **cut.yml should set it.**
- `--dry-run` still prints the whole plan, with the queue in the order the lanes pull it. On this tree that is 2 builds, 1019 queued steps and ~60 alone steps.

## The named alone list (`lanes::ISOLATED`) and why

These are the targets whose tests assert on wall-clock time, so a busy neighbour could turn them red. They were found by grepping the suites for `recv_timeout`, `deadline`, `Instant`/`elapsed` and `Duration::from_secs`. Suites that only print a timing are not listed.

- `app:lib` and `kernel:lib`: watchdogs in the libs' own tests (`step_guard_tests`, `step_division_tests`, `solidcore_step`)
- `app:import_step_closed_shell`, `import_step_corner_blend`, `import_step_curve_guard`, `import_step_guard`, `import_step_guard_default_cap`, `import_step_open_shell`: STEP import watchdogs (`within(limit, ..)` panics on a timeout)
- `app:large_models` (streaming import < 60 s), `mcp_live` (TCP deadlines of 0.3-20 s), `shoulder_adaptive` (< 60 s), `step_nesting` (refusal < 1 s), `stock_field_cost` (per-program budget), `stock_play`, `stock_play_partial`, `stock_play_precalc` (worker deadlines)
- `kernel:heal_import`, `import_corpus`, `mesh_deviation_bench`, `solidcraft_hostile`, `solidcraft_import`, `step_agreement`, `step_import`: built on the `step_util` / `smb_util` watchdogs

A new suite with a wall-clock assertion has to be added to this list. A test pins that every listed binary exists.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p xtask`: all pass (161 unit tests plus the integration binaries). These tests were rewritten for the queue: lanes (schedule split, the ISOLATED entries exist, target keys, longest-first order, history picks the newest release `timings.tsv`), the executor fixture (overlap, failure, build stop, VOID), and budget (the per-lane `-j` and test-thread sums stay within the budget, and alone steps get the full budget).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not exercised: a full release gate run. That is the measurement in the comment to follow.

## Risks

- More app/kernel binaries now run beside each other, so peak memory is higher (the app heavy release lanes especially). The suites already use per-process temp dirs (`std::process::id()`), and that was spot-checked.
- A timing-sensitive test missed by the grep could flake under load. Adding it to `ISOLATED` fixes that.

## Revert

Revert this commit. The plan steps themselves are unchanged, so nothing else depends on it. To get back only the old alone rule, make `lanes::alone` return true for any `camcraft-app` / `camcraft-kernel` argument.

`PROCESS_VERSION` is not bumped here; the merging session bumps it.

title: fix(chamfer): no-pick 2D Chamfer rides the wall; verify holds its tip to it
body:
## What changed

**Generator (no-pick 2D Chamfer).** The ride sectioned the model at Top of Part Z and put the cone tip on that outline at the corner depth. On a model whose edge already carries a modelled chamfer, that outline is the bevel's *top* edge, which sits inside the wall by the bevel's width. The cone then cut a V 0.71 mm into the part (QA p01-flange: `G1 X75 Y15.999 Z-3`, which is world y -14.001 against a wall at y -15), and the width moved only Z. Now `material_source` sections the source twice, at the top plane (the edges to break) and at the corner depth `top - width*tan(angle)` (the wall). The new `machining2d::chamfer_ride_loops` gives each top loop the wall loop within `width` of it. For a vertical wall the two loops are the same and the top loop itself is ridden, so sharp-edged parts post exactly as before. A top edge with no wall within the width (a blind pocket or island shallower than the chamfer depth) is refused by name, with the spot.

**Verify (program sim).** The V passed because the op's edge-break record declared that same false edge, and any declared bevel got credit. A 2D Chamfer's records are now credited only where the cone tip stands on a wall: at every sample along the edge, the model's top 0.05 mm off the edge, on at least one side, must be no higher than the tip plus the verdict tolerance (`sim::stock_sim::on_walls`, new `wall_anchor.rs`). A record that fails is dropped and logged, and its columns are judged against the model, so the cut is a blocking gouge. Deburr records are not held to this: a deburr may legitimately break an obtuse 3D edge, such as a drafted wall. `program_breaks` moved from `stock_sim.rs` to `stock_sim_breaks.rs`, and `Planned` gained `walled`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/2435-chamfer-modelled-edge.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, each mutation-checked:
- `crates/app/tests/chamfer_modelled_edge.rs` (new). The model is a 40x20x10 brick with a modelled 1x45 chamfer on its top edges. It is the stock and the part, and one no-pick 2D Chamfer runs on it.
  - `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_a_modelled_chamfer_rides_the_wall`: width 1. Every feed tip is at z 9 on the wall (x ±20 / y ±10), and the gate is clean.
  - `the_width_moves_the_tip_along_the_bevel_not_only_in_z`: width 0.5. Tips are at z 9.5 on the bevel (±19.5 / ±9.5), and the gate is clean.
  - `a_cone_tip_inside_the_part_is_a_gouge_not_edge_break_credit`: the old ride and its record are put back by hand, and the gate must report a gouge.
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests` (4 unit tests: vertical wall unchanged, bevel rides the wall, too-far wall refuses, lower edge ignored).
- `stock_sim::wall_anchor::tests` (2 unit tests: tip on the wall keeps its credit, tip inside loses it).

Mutations:
- Generator fix reverted (ride the top section again): the two ride tests fail. With the fixed verify, the old ride is convicted end to end: `gouge ... 1175 cell(s), worst 0.94 mm`.
- Wall filter disabled (`walled` ignored): the gouge test fails, because the gate passes the V.

QA part (p01-flange, from the issue), run through `camcraft-cli process`:
- No-pick width 1 now posts `X75 Y15 Z-3` (world y -15, z 14), with the gate ok.
- Width 0.5 posts `Y15.5 Z-2.5`, with the gate ok.
- The old ride, with this verify, is blocked: `gouge ... worst 1.00 mm` (w 1) and `worst 0.50 mm` (w 0.5).
- The issue's picked-chain workaround project still posts, with the gate ok.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` : green, 215 steps, 0 failed (17.4 min), among them chamfer_modelled_edge, edge_break_gate, edge_break_bound, golden_cl, mill2d_b, setup_align_chamfer, setup_carry_credits, stock_chamfer_added_part, posting, solid_law_goldens, verify, and the motion and sim lib unit tests, plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The tilted (3+2) frame variant of the no-pick chamfer. The corner depth is taken in the frame's own Z, the same as the top plane, but no tilted test was added.
- Curved bevels (a modelled round under a chamfer) beyond the QA STEP's R5 corners.

title: fix(sim): pack the playback picture's base from the uncut stock
body:
## What changed

The simulation's stock body was never visible in v0.23.0 (#2396).

**Cause.** #2181 (the stock removal calculated before playback) moved the playback worker's `PackedBase::of` call after the calculation. The calculation leaves the playback at the end of the program. `PackedBase::of` runs the eikonal pass, which writes `max(mesh, cut)` into the mesh layer, and later frames can only lift cells over it. So the GPU eye's base was the **finished** part, and every frame at every playhead drew the finished part. When a program machines the part to size, that body sits inside the model, so no stock is seen.

**Fix.** `crates/app/src/stock_play_worker.rs`: the base is packed from the uncut stock before the calculation runs, as it was before #2181. This is a one-line move with a comment. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2396-sim-stock-visible.md`.

## How tested

- Pinning test `crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs::the_picture_at_the_start_is_the_uncut_stock_after_the_calculation`. It spawns the worker with the calculation, waits for `Ready` and takes the packed frame at move 0. It asserts that the composed lattice the eye draws (`max(base.mesh, cut) < 0`) holds the uncut stock's material, and that the base mesh layer is the uncut stock's bit for bit.
  - Before the fix: FAILED, `move 0 draws the uncut stock, not the finished part`, left 2016 (the finished part's texels), right 2880 (the uncut stock's).
  - After the fix: ok.
- The whole `stock_play_precalc` suite passes (8 pass, 1 heavy lane ignored).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 4481c2a06: green (app lib, stock_play, stock_play_partial, stock_play_precalc; 5 steps, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

- The windowed app on a GPU. The test reads the packed lattice the GPU eye uploads, not pixels, so the shader composite is not run.
- The maintainer's own project. The fixture is the #2181 suite's staged face with a part cube, where the finished stock equals the part.
- No pixel snapshots were run or changed.

title: fix(app): every operation's approach starts over the setup's WCS origin
body:
## What changed

Most mill generators seed their path at X0 Y0 on the clearance plane. That point is the world origin. The opening rapid started there, so these items read the world origin and not G54:
- the viewport (the drawn approach);
- the simulation link between operations;
- the CL `START` line;
- the post engine's `StartX/Y/Z`.

The posted move blocks were already correct, because a post writes only the end of each move.

The fix:
- New `Toolpath::seat_approach` (`crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs`). When the first move is a rapid that leaves the seed, the start of that rapid moves to the WCS origin (X/Y) on the same plane. The end of the rapid does not change.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` calls it after generation. The call comes before the yaw exit, the fixture routing and the verify laws, so those laws judge the new rapid. The origin comes from `wcs_context`, which is the same origin that the post subtracts. A 3+2 path reads the origin in its local frame (`TiltedFrame::to_local`).
- These paths do not change: paths that open at their own first point (holes, plasma, sinker, lathe, wire, rotary, 3D roughing, adaptive trochoidal), and a zero-length seed rapid.

The cause has existed since 942a36d65 (#690 / #697, v0.17). It is not a 0.23 regression. The reproduction and the family list are on #2382.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2382-wcs-start.md`.

## Readings

- Reporter's project (local copy, not attached): each operation opened with a rapid from X0 Y0 at the clearance height. G54 is at a stock corner far from that point. The project does not post, because of a correct refusal that is not related to this issue (Home after Pause).
- Fixture (G54 at X40 Y20 Z10.5): on main, the face and the parallel finish start at (0, 0, 30). With the fix, they start at (40, 20, 30).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs`:
  - `a_2d_operation_starts_over_the_wcs_origin` (fails on main)
  - `a_3d_operation_starts_over_the_wcs_origin` (fails on main)
  - `a_hole_operation_starts_over_its_first_hole`

title: fix(operation): read a tilted op's reference heights along its tool axis
body:
## What changed

A tilted (3+1 / 3+2, `tilt.a_deg`/`b_deg`) operation took its reference heights - Top/Bottom of stock, Top/Bottom of model, Work offset - as the setup's world Z and only subtracted the plane origin's Z. It never measured along the turned tool axis. On #2389's bar (10 Y x 30 Z, centred on A) a Slot at A 90 with Top = Top of stock got 15 along the axis instead of 5, so it cut air. On other sides of an asymmetric stock it would plunge to the wrong depth.

- New `camcraft_app::operation::fold_height` (`crates/app/src/operation/tilt_heights.rs`). Under a non-upright tilt, each reference height is the referenced geometry's extent along the tool axis (`TiltedFrame::z_local` over its facets). It is returned as `z_local + origin.z`, so the existing `- origin.z` fold in `run_job` / `source_region` gives exactly the local value.
- Where it is used: the generation heights (`collect_job` through `resolve_params_folded`), the Contour/Pocket/Trace section plane (`section_z_of`) and the area-controls cut plane (`boundary_ctx`).
- Unchanged: Fixed heights keep the shipped `h - origin.z` law (pinned by `tilt.rs`). A Selection reference keeps the setup resolve, because a tilted op refuses a picked source first. Untilted ops and upright tilts (A0 B0) read the setup resolve verbatim, so prismatic paths and goldens keep their bits.
- `resolve_params` now delegates to `resolve_params_with` (the resolver is passed in). The refusal wording is unchanged.
- The viewport planes and the Heights tab's "(= Z ...)" echo are display-only and were split out to #2416 (P3, filed). Decision record: `docs/decisions/2389-tilt-heights-axis.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, in the new file `crates/app/tests/tilt_heights.rs`:
- `a_slot_at_a90_reads_top_of_stock_along_the_tool_axis`: the issue's proof. Clearance along the axis is 15 (main gives 25) and the bottom is 4.
- `an_offset_bar_reads_its_own_side_at_a_minus_90_and_the_underside`: an asymmetric stock (Y -1..11, Z -20..10) with a plane origin off the world origin.
  - A -90, origin (2,0,3): top 11; clearance 21 along the axis (main gives 17).
  - A0 B180, origin Z 3: top 23. This case also exercises the `+ origin.z` hand-off.
- `a_tilted_contour_sections_the_model_along_the_tool_axis`: a tilted Contour on a part, with Top/Bottom of model. On main it is refused with "no material at z = 14.000"; with the fix it contours at local 4..3.

Mutation check (revert, then restore):
- `collect_job` set back to the setup resolve: tests 1 and 2 go red (25 vs 15; 17 vs 21).
- `section_z_of` given no frame: test 3 goes red.
- `+ origin.z` dropped from `fold_height`: test 2 goes red (18 vs 21).
- With everything restored, all three are green.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 247 steps, 0 failed (14.6 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. It includes `first_4axis_part`, which holds `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` and `.nc` byte-for-byte (the round bar is symmetric about A, so it stays unchanged), plus `tilt`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `opframe_seam` and the heights suites.

## Not exercised

- The UI planes and echo (#2416).
- The post's `ClearancePlane` parameter for a tilted op still states the setup Z (`posting.rs`).
- `material_local.top` is still `material.top - origin.z`.
- A tilt at a non-right angle (e.g. A 45) on a round bar: the facet extent is the tessellation's, which can be up to one chord sagitta under the true cylinder.
- Bore/Thread under a tilt: they read the same height set, but no test covers them.
- No machine run.

Changelog: A tilted (3+2) operation now measures Top/Bottom of stock, Top/Bottom of model and Work offset heights along its tool axis, not as the setup's Z (#2389)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #2389 (the viewport planes and "(= Z ...)" text, #2416, finish it)

body:
## What changed
- The machine list and the post list come from a scan of their folders. They no longer come from the fixed `MACHINES` and `BUILTINS` tables.

- A table entry shows only if its file is present. A removed file does not leave an entry.
- The Refresh buttons scan the folder again (`posting::rescan`). The machine page and the post picker have a Refresh button. The AccessKit names are "Refresh machine list" and "Refresh post list".
- A malformed file does not stop the scan. It is listed with its own refusals.
- A document that needs a missing post or machine is still refused by name (#2319).
- The MCP machine-name list uses the same scan.
- The post combo finds the document's post by name (`posting::post_name`) in the scanned list (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_pick.rs`). It never indexes past the list. A post whose file is gone shows its own name with "(file missing)". The document's post does not change. The Setup Post page shows why the post folder did not read (`FolderScan::problem`).
- The folder listing is `camcraft_post::data_dir::list_files`. The scan is `camcraft_post::data_scan::scan_folder` (and `FolderScan`). `app` re-exports the two from `posting`.
- The process cache (`post_scan`, `machine_scan`, `rescan`, `scan_reads`) is in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`. It binds the scan to the `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` tables and to the process folders, which are in that file. No new file in `crates/app/src`. No new dependency between our crates.

## Root cause
The lists were built from `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`. The UI pickers and `machine/library.rs` `builtins()` read those tables. No code read the folder.

title: feat(post): wrapped A on the Tormach microARC 4 (G93, cumulative A)
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` no longer refuses an A that changes inside an operation on an A-about-X machine. It now posts it as wrapped (simultaneous) A, based on mkinney's four PathPilot Hub readings on #796 (v2.14.4, 770MX SIM, 4th axis on):

- **A is cumulative.** PathPilot treats A as plain degrees with no rollover (A350 -> `G1 A10` turned back 340 deg). Each target is the nearest equivalent of the held angle: 179 -> 181, 359 -> 361, never back through 0. A count past the stated travel is refused by name.
- **A turning X Y Z feed is G93.** `F = 1 / t`, where t (min) = max((the tip's path relative to the part + one rounding step) / the programmed feed, the posted |dA| / the stated A rate). F is floored to 0.001, so rounding only ever slows a move. Neither the cutting feed nor the A rate is exceeded. The rate comes from `rotaryRate` (#885).
- **An A-only feed stays G94**, with F in deg/min under the same time law (Hub reading 4). Feeds that don't turn A are unchanged. G94 is restated before any motion that is not a G93 feed and at every section end.
- **Turning moves are split onto their segment.** The machine moves XYZ in a line while A turns, so the tip relative to the part bows off the stream's segment. Each turning move (rapids too) is split into 2^k pieces until the bow is within 0.005 mm (at most 256 pieces, else refused by name).
- **A is reset between operations:** as before (#785), each section restates its first A as -180..180 after `G53 G0 Z0`, so a wrap that ended at A300 unwinds at the top of Z.
- **Refused by name:** a machine file with no A rate ("states no A feed rate"), a count past the travel ("A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over)"), an arc / canned cycle / probe move that would turn A, a turning move from an unknown start, and a move that still bows after 256 splits.
- `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` now states A `max_normal_speed` 360 deg/min. That is the rate the Hub ran as asked. It is conservative: no Tormach rate could be cited with confidence.
- Docs: the tester-kit README, `first-4axis-part.md` and `continuous-4-axis.md` (with its site test), plus `docs/decisions/796-tormach-wrapped-a.md`. The kit's `.camproj` was re-saved by its own test, so it carries the A rate.

Fork branch based on upstream `main` at 4e8616b (not a cut tag), so the #885 rule and the current post are in.

## How tested

New pins in `crates/app/tests/tormach_wrapped_a.rs` (10 tests):
- `a_long_xyz_move_takes_its_time_from_the_feed`: `G93 G1 X50 Y0 Z0 A1 F11.999` (50 mm at F600)
- `a_mostly_rotary_move_takes_its_time_from_the_a_rate`: `G1 X51 Y0 Z0 A91 F4` (90 deg at 360 deg/min)
- `g94_comes_back_before_an_xyz_only_feed_and_a_turns_in_deg_per_min`
- `a_counts_on_through_180_and_360_never_back_through_0`
- `the_next_operation_resets_a_at_the_safe_z`
- `a_section_that_ends_in_g93_restates_g94_before_m5`
- `a_turning_move_off_the_axis_is_split_onto_its_chord`: every posted point, turned back into the part, lies on the stream's chord, and each piece is held to both rates
- `a_count_past_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`, `a_machine_with_no_a_rate_is_refused_by_name`, `the_microarc_states_its_a_rate`

Golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc` is the microARC kit's job plus a real Rotary Parallel (1/8" ball) on the bar. It is pinned by `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, which replaces `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_is_refused_by_name` and also checks A unwrapping, G93 on every turning XYZ feed, G94 elsewhere, and G94 at the section end.

Updated: `tormach_fourth_axis::an_a_that_changes_inside_an_operation_posts_wrapped_a` (was `..._is_refused`). In `fourth_axis_pose`, the two fanuc tests on the microARC file now place A with a rapid first, because that file now states an A rate and the #885 rule asks for it. The recorded `rotary.refusal` golden for tormach (tilt-head machine) now names the B tilt refusal instead.

Gate (macOS, debug, targeted - `cargo xtask gate quick` plans every app suite because a new golden is shared test input, so the touched suites ran instead): every camcraft-app test binary that names Tormach / the microARC (69 binaries, incl. `tormach_wrapped_a`, `microarc_test_part`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `first_4axis_part`, `index_swing`, `tormach_post`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `recorded_post_streams`) and every camcraft-post binary that names Tormach or the recorded streams (45 binaries, incl. `script_tormach`, `explain_tormach`, `recorded_streams`): all green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app` on the four changed test files `-D warnings`: clean. `site/tests/test_first_4axis_part.py`: the updated tests pass; `test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones` fails the same way on upstream main (machine name not in `posting.rs`), not touched here.

## Not exercised

- No real cut, and this exact program has not been run in the Hub. The readings cover single test moves only.
- PathPilot's A soft limits. The file keeps -360..360, and a wrap past it is refused.

## Hub check (before trusting it on the 770MX + microARC 4)

Run slowly (feed override 25-50 %, single block for the first lines), with the tool lifted 1" above the work offset (air cut):
1. Post the golden's WRAP op (or `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) and load it in the Hub 770MX SIM with the 4th axis on. Confirm it loads with no error on `G93` / `G94` lines and no "F word missing".
2. Watch the A DRO on a stretch that passes 180 (e.g. line 1393 of the golden, A180 -> A185.757): A must keep counting up, never swing back through 0.
3. Time one long G93 line against its F (time = 1/F min). Check one A-only `G1 A.. F360` runs at 6 deg/s.
4. Confirm the control is back in G94 after the WRAP op (Status tab / the next op's feeds run at their ipm).
5. Check PathPilot's A soft limits (jog A past +360 / -360 in the SIM) and report them on #796, so the machine file's travel can be stated.
6. Only then air-cut on the real machine at a low override, the bar in the chuck, a hand on feed hold.

Changelog: Tormach PathPilot post: continuous (wrapped) A on the microARC 4 - A counts on past 360, turning feeds in G93 held to the feed and the stated A rate (360 deg/min); refused by name when the machine states no A rate or the count passes the A travel (#796)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #796

- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight.rs` (`HighlightCache`) to resolve selected, hovered, and row-hovered outlines once per state change.
- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight_mesh.rs` to tessellate each highlight layer into one cached `egui::Shape::Mesh` in `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel`.
- Added `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs` and `crates/ui/src/panel_cache.rs` on `State` to cache world vertices, cutting regions and outlines, toolpath overlay lines, non-transient `world::Scene` plus digest, Geometry chips, 3-2-1 datum checks, selection account, unresolved notes, operation status banners, and browser operation rows.

- On models with many chains or facets, `features_of` re-hashed triangle buffers and `resolve_chain` re-walked and split chains repeatedly during frame, highlight, and panel queries.

title: fix(tools): a refused tool names itself and the rule it breaks
body:
#1186: the project loader refused a tool with bad numbers. The message was `tool parameters are not usable: ToolDto { ... }`, with the full structure. The refusal was correct, but it did not name the tool or the field. `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` printed a similar dump. The library import and the library reader gave a general message.

The branch has upstream main at a529c455, merged in.

## What changed

- **`Tool::why_not_sane() -> Option<String>`** (new file `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`). It gives the first rule that a tool breaks, in plain words. Examples:
  - `turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min (it must be over 0)`
  - `corner radius 100 mm is more than half the 6 mm diameter`
  - `a drill's tip angle 50 degrees must be over 60`
  - `a sinker electrode turns no spindle: its spindle speed must be 0, not 1000 rpm`
  - `TurningData::why_not_sane` gives the same for the turning limits.
- **One source of truth.** `Tool::is_sane` and `TurningData::is_sane` are now `why_not_sane().is_none()`. Thus the message and the verdict cannot be different. The rules moved out of `tools.rs` in the same order, with the same limits.
- **The rules that main added are included.** Main added these after the branch started:
  - the `pitch_min` field;
  - the waterjet, electrode and thread-mill kinds and their rules;
  - the catalog and cutting-row refusals.
  - Each of these rules has its own message now.
- **Four refusals now read `tool '<name>': <rule>`:**
  - the project loader (`project/validate.rs`), which is the case in the issue;
  - `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` (`commands/tool.rs`);
  - the tool-library import (`commands/tool_import.rs`);
  - the library reader (`tool_library.rs`).
  - The MCP tools `add_tool` and `edit_tool` use the same commands. Thus an agent also gets the named rule.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1186-tool-refusal-names.md`.

## Tests

New pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/project_tool_refusal.rs` opens a saved file with one bad field through the real loader (`project::open`).
  - `a_bad_turning_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: surface speed 0, a negative feed per rev, and a max rpm below the rpm of the tool.
  - `a_bad_milling_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: a corner radius more than half the diameter, and feed 0.
  - The two tests also make sure that the message has no `ToolDto` dump.
- `tools::tool_sanity::tests`:
  - `a_turning_field_is_named`, `a_milling_field_is_named` and `the_newer_kinds_are_named`.
  - `the_named_law_gives_the_old_verdict_everywhere` keeps the `is_sane` body of main as an oracle. It also keeps the `TurningData::is_sane` body.
  - The test examines each catalog tool as each of the 18 kinds (Wire added at the merge of 2026-11-18). It sets each of the 14 numeric fields to 13 edge values: 0, negative, the 60 and 180 degree limits, more than 500, NaN and infinity. It also examines flute counts, orientation codes and turning data.
  - The new law gives the same verdict in all cases. Thus no tool changes from accepted to refused, or from refused to accepted.
  - `a_bad_wire_is_named` (added at the merge of 2026-11-18): an EDM wire with a spindle speed, a diameter out of range or a corner radius is refused, and the message names the wire and the rule.
  - `a_valid_wire_is_accepted` (added at the merge of 2026-11-18): a wire with rpm 0 and a diameter of 0.02, 0.25 or 1 mm is accepted.

Changed test: `tool_cutter_params::a_reshape_is_refused_by_name_against_the_new_numbers` looked for the old text "finite and positive". It now looks for `tool '<name>': diameter -1 mm is outside`.

Gates on dbf7799e:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green.
  - The tools step ran the lib tests and `waterjet`.
  - The app step ran the lib tests and 44 suites. These include all `tool_*` suites, `project_tool_refusal`, `project_roundtrip`, `thread_mill`, `waterjet_machine`, `plasma_profile`, `mcp` and `commands_undo`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

- The UI shows these refusals in the status line, as before. No UI test reads their text. A search of `crates/ui` finds none of the old messages.
- A missing or unknown field is a serde parse error. It occurs before this law runs. The serde message already names the field, and it does not change.

Changelog: A tool refused for unusable numbers (project load, add or edit tool, library import) now names the tool and the rule it breaks, e.g. "tool 'T1': turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min", instead of printing the whole definition (#1186)

Effort: low (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #1186

title: feat(ui): drag rings in Rotate mode turn the selected part
body:
Stacked on #1330. This branch starts from the head of #1330 (`58df4b729`, fork branch `mkinney:issue/1198-drag-to-move`) with `origin/main` merged in. Until #1330 merges, the diff shows the commits of #1330 too. The new work is commit `043b7e0a9`.

## What changed
- The viewport bar has a new Rotate button after Move. Move and Rotate are mutually exclusive. A toggle cancels the live drag of the other mode.
- With Rotate on, the one selected part shows three rings round its bounding-box centre. Each ring is square to one shown axis. The ring radius is a constant 60 px on the screen. A press within 6 px of a ring grabs the nearest ring.
- The drag angle is the point where the cursor ray meets the ring plane, measured about the centre. The angle is unwrapped, so a drag can go past 180 degrees. During the drag the part preview turns and the bar shows `Turn about Z: +35.0°`. The world does not change during the drag.
- The release queues one `CommandKind::TurnModelBy { name, axis, angle_rad }`. The drain runs the existing `MoveModel`, so the turn is one undo step. The generated operations go stale and the stock follows the part, as for a typed turn.
- An aligned setup turns the part about the axis that the user sees (the turn goes back through the setup alignment).
- Escape cancels the turn with no history step. A turn that ends at its start angle queues nothing and writes no rotation noise (#2177).
- A bad axis, a non-finite angle or a missing part is refused by name on the status line.
- New files: `crates/ui/src/turn_drag.rs` (the drag law), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turn_handles.rs` (the paint), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar_tests.rs` (the bar tests moved out to keep `viewport_bar.rs` near 400 lines).
- No new app command, so no new MCP tool. MCP `move_model` already sets the rotation.

## How the stale path is pinned
`body_turn::a_ring_drag_is_one_undoable_turn_that_stales_the_path_and_carries_the_stock` drags the Z ring on the seeded document. Before the drag, `camcraft_app::posting::program_ops` returns `Ok`. After the release, it returns an `Err` that contains "regenerate", so the post refuses. One undo makes the history clean again and `program_ops` returns `Ok` again. The same test checks that the stock box still holds the turned part. The app-level pin `crates/app/tests/commands_undo.rs::a_moved_part_marks_generated_ops_stale_and_undo_clears_it` already covers a pure rotation in the stale stamp.

## Pinning tests
- `egui_app::tests::body_turn::*` (5 tests): rings only in Rotate mode at a constant size; one undoable turn that makes the path stale and carries the stock; Escape cancels; a zero turn adds nothing; empty space still orbits.
- `turn_drag_tests::*` (6 tests): the angle under the cursor, a drag past half a turn, no command for a press off the rings or a turn in place, the centre stays in place, a turned setup, refusals by name.
- `egui_app::viewport_bar::tests::move_and_rotate_modes_never_share_the_part`.

## Readings
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on head `043b7e0a9`: ui lib 954 passed, 1 failed; boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_files, waterjet_tool all green. The one failure is `stock_fit_controls_follow_the_selected_shape`, which also fails on main (#2170, fix PR #2171).
- Clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised
- No hand test in the live window. The screenshots come from the kittest harness render of the shipping shell with the GPU viewport, at 1280x720.
- No angle snapping (not asked for; see `docs/decisions/2047-drag-to-rotate.md`).
- `shell.rs` was already longer than 400 lines before this change; this PR adds 11 lines to it.

## Screenshots
Before (Move mode of #1330 on this branch: the move balls, no rings):
![before move](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/before-move.png?raw=true)
After (Rotate mode, a Z-ring drag of +35 degrees in progress):
![after rotate](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/after-rotate.png?raw=true)

Changelog: The viewport bar has a Rotate mode: drag a ring on the selected part to turn it about an axis through its centre, as one undo step.
Effort: high

Fixes #2047

title: feat(post): 1-based script errors, loop limits, blank template and preview samples
body:
**Stacked on #468** (branch `issue/419-thread-dips`, head `d3bb673d`): both change `Script::load`. Only commit `236d40d6` is this issue's work; review that commit. Retarget/refresh after #468 merges.

## What changed (crates/post only)
- Host prelude, rotary and explanation helpers are evaluated separately from user source (`host.js` / `user.cps`), so syntax and runtime errors report the user's own 1-based line and column, with no prelude offset.
- Sandbox limits: Boa loop limit 1,000,000 iterations, recursion 64, stack 4,096, kept for every hook call; same on desktop and wasm. A post run is capped at 100,000 output lines counted across hooks; the buffer length is checked in Rust before it is reported or drained, so direct buffer writes cannot slip an oversized program through. Each limit is a named refusal.
- Host prelude moved to `js_host.rs` (re-exported from `js`, public paths unchanged) to keep `js.rs` under 400 lines (386).
- New `post::preview`: `BLANK_TEMPLATE` (original, empty hooks, emits nothing), `DEFAULT_VMC_JSON`, and `SAMPLES` - four deterministic sample streams (facing, contour, pocket, drill) built from committed goldens with setup/operation/tool/spindle/clearance records.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/2069-post-sandbox.md`. No new crate dependency.

## Pins
- `camcraft-post --test script_sandbox` (10): `syntax_errors_report_exact_user_line_and_column`, `runtime_errors_report_exact_user_line_and_column`, `endless_top_level_loop_is_refused`, `endless_hook_loop_is_refused`, `excessive_recursion_is_refused`, `excessive_stack_is_refused`, `output_limit_counts_lines_across_hooks`, `output_limit_covers_every_line_writer`, `direct_output_buffer_writes_are_refused_before_drain`, `direct_output_buffer_writes_are_refused_at_run_boundary`.
- `camcraft-post --test post_preview` (3): `blank_template_compiles_and_emits_no_lines_or_warnings`, `preview_samples_post_cleanly_and_deterministically`, `preview_samples_carry_setup_operation_tool_spindle_and_cycle_feed`.
All 13 pass on `236d40d6` (macOS, m3). The worker checked each pin with a mutation (red without the fix, green with it).

## Known inherited failures (not caused by this PR)
The quick gate shows two failures that come from #468's older base:
- `camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting troubleshooting_messages_still_exist_in_the_sources` - panics at `docs_troubleshooting.rs:83` ("troubleshooting page is readable: NotFound"). Fixed on main by PR #2053.
- `camcraft-app --test operations threaded_batch_matches_the_serial_loop_bit_for_bit` - panics at `operations.rs:1433`: APocket3D refuses BN-0600 (the pocket is 20 mm deep but the wider shank starts 15 mm above the tip).

Evidence: both tests were run on #468's head `d3bb673d` with this PR's changes stashed (clean tree, `git status` empty) and both failed with the same messages. This PR changes only `crates/post`; it does not touch the troubleshooting docs or the 3D pocket shank check. Neither failure is fixed here, because the fix belongs on #468's refresh from main (not pushed to #468's branch from this PR).

- The UI Post Editor preview wiring (this PR provides the engine-side pieces only).
- wasm build of the limits (same Boa settings, not built here).
- Full quick gate beyond the touched post suites and the two app tests above.

Fork synced at its current main (upstream merge `09366f64e`).

title: refactor(log): library and UI diagnostics become tracing events
body:
## What changed

The last slice of #163, after PR #222 (app seams: save/open/post/generate/commands) and PR #969 (app library eprintln!s and the budget-refusal events). With this, no diagnostic in the library or UI crates bypasses the one `tracing` subscriber any more.

- **Library crates** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): every non-test `eprintln!` is now a `tracing` event - refusals and fallbacks at `warn` (refused move/builder axis or C angle; multi-axis moves held vertical or radial, a rotary start on the axis, a degenerate drive curve skipped; a non-finite sim path left out or move held still; the dual iso-surface falling back to marching tetrahedra; a missing starter tool catalog), the opt-in `CAMCRAFT_PROFILE_PROJECTION` profile lines at `info`. The text of each line is unchanged.
- **Standalone bins** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): each installs a stderr subscriber with the app's filter rule (`CAMCRAFT_LOG`, else `RUST_LOG`, else `info`), so the converted library warnings still reach their terminal. Their own `println!` reports and usage errors are the CLI's answer and stay as they are.
- **UI**: the `diag` seam (#31) now emits `tracing` events natively (target `camcraft_ui`, `warn`/`info`) instead of `eprintln!`/`println!`; wasm32 still goes to the browser console. The native window (`shell_window.rs`, `shell_window/frame.rs`), GPU bring-up (`gpu_init.rs`), Cmd+Q hook (`os_quit.rs`) and the headless proof (`shell.rs`) now speak through the seam, so the law test's allow-list shrinks to the seam and test-only code (`gpu.rs`'s test module, `headless_gpu.rs`'s `device_for_test`, whose "SKIPPED - NOT a pass" line must show in a test run with no subscriber).

**Dependencies.** No new crate: `tracing` and `tracing-subscriber` are already workspace dependencies (root `Cargo.toml`, since PR #222) and in `Cargo.lock`; this PR adds `{ workspace = true }` lines for them to the five library crates and `tracing` (plus `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency) to `camcraft-ui`. `Cargo.lock` gains only those dependency edges. No `camcraft-*` edge is added. Decision record: `docs/decisions/163-tracing-libs.md`.

The issue's "Done means" is now covered across the three PRs: post writes name the file and result or why not (#222), a generation budget names its limit (#969, `a_budget_refusal_names_the_limit_that_fired_at_warn`), levels come from `CAMCRAFT_LOG`/`RUST_LOG` with a quiet `info` default (#222), and the library/UI prints that bypassed the filter are gone (this PR). No event was added inside a hot loop (the geometry profile lines stay behind their env var).

## How tested

- New pinning tests:
  - `camcraft-cl` `tests/refusal_log.rs::a_refused_axis_or_angle_is_a_warning_under_the_cl_target` - a refused move axis, C angle and builder axis are each a `WARN` event under `camcraft_cl`, and a stricter filter silences them.
  - `camcraft-ui` `diag::tests::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` - `diag_warn!`/`diag_info!` are `WARN`/`INFO` events under `camcraft_ui`, and a filter below them stays quiet.
  - `camcraft-ui` `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam` (existing law, allow-list tightened).
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`; Cargo changes fall back to batch scope): green on every test step in 27.9 min (geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui suites all ok). The clippy step fails only on the pre-existing `MIN_LABEL_PX is never used` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` (upstream main, #2104, not touched here); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings -A dead_code` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The wasm32 build of the UI was not run (the diag wasm branch is unchanged).
- The real GPU window and the Windows GUI-subsystem console were not launched by hand; the converted lines are the same text through the same seam.
- Pre-existing, not from this PR: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on upstream main at 780b0a25a with `constant MIN_LABEL_PX is never used` (painted.rs:115, after PR #2095). Filed as #2104 (P2).

title: feat(tools)!: a tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.
- UI: with a referenced holder the tool settings show the holder diameter and length the laws read as text, not as two fields. The Profile tab names the entry and the picker shows it. The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2016-holder-reference.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (tools, app and ui suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. macOS (m5).

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`
  - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`: for every library entry, at the default and at other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, envelope, band stack, stamp term and facets equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored, also after a save and load.
  - `an_older_project_loads_as_custom_holders_with_the_same_collision_result`: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings (the BT30 flange strikes the fixture wall, hit for hit).
  - `an_older_tool_library_loads_as_custom_holders_and_a_new_one_round_trips_the_reference`
  - `an_unknown_entry_refuses_the_file_by_name_and_never_lands_another_holder` (project and `.camtools`)
  - `a_library_holder_is_the_reference_in_the_document_and_the_file`
  - `the_unchanged_outline_keeps_the_reference_and_an_edited_point_makes_it_custom`
  - `mcp_set_tool_holder_writes_the_reference`
- `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs` unit tests.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_holder_reference.rs`: `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`, `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux. The release tier and the pixel-snapshot lanes (no snapshot PNG changed).
- No real v0.21.0 file was read: the older file in the tests is this build's file rewritten to the older form (`body` with the drawn copy, version 61 / 1).
- The app was not driven by hand.

## Notes for the reviewer

- A build of main between #1453 and this change reads v62 and would drop the `holder` key (development builds only; v0.21.0 refuses v62).
- A corrected library entry now reaches every project that names it. A copy kept the old numbers.
- The tool record's `holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten by the entry (they are what the tool goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move the stamp). The settings show the entry's numbers.

Changelog: A tool's library holder is stored as a reference to the library entry (name, gauge length, projection) in the project and tool library files, not as a drawn copy; the tool settings show the entry's holder size. Breaking: v0.21.0 and older refuse a file that names a library holder.

Effort: max (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: a project or tool library saved with a library holder states it as a reference (project v62, `.camtools` version 2); v0.21.0 and older refuse such a file.

Process change: yes
