title: feat(tools)!: cutting data by work material - Unknown default row, stepdown/stepover, stock material
body:
## What changed

Tool cutting data by work material (#2015, part of #2007):

- **`Unknown` row.** Every tool's cutting data now holds an `Unknown` row (file word `unknown`; in code `CuttingRow::material == None`). It is what the tool runs when no row names the material in force, and the fallback for a row's missing stepdown/stepover. It is derived from the tool's own rpm/feed and stored only when it states something more (other numbers, or a step) - so a new tool has it, every older tool reads its own numbers as it, and plain tools are stored, saved and shown to MCP byte for byte as before. A command that moves the running numbers away from a derived row stores it first. A waterjet (recipes) and an electrode (rpm 0) get none, so a sane tool never turns insane.
- **Stepdown and stepover per row** (mm, optional). They seed an operation's stepdown/stepover only inside an undoable command (quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the feature recognizer, `SetWorkMaterial`, `SetStockMaterial`, retargeting a tool), never on load. Seeded kinds: pocket, adaptive, offset, slot, 3-D pocket, multi-axis rough, face (stepover; stepdown only when staged), 2-D contour (stepdown). A stepover wider than the cutter is refused by tool name.
- **Setup stock material.** New `StockMaterial` component on a setup's stock and the undoable `SetStockMaterial` command (MCP `set_stock_material`, stock page "Material" group). The row is picked by the stock's material, then the document's, then `Unknown`. The tools' running rpm/feed (the posted S word) follow the document material only - a tool is shared by every setup.
- **`.camtools`/project migration.** `PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63 (the issue's "61 to 62" predates #1453's bump). A v62 project loads with each tool's own rpm/feed as its `Unknown` row; nothing it runs moves. `.camtools` reader accepts versions 1, 2 and 3; the writer writes 3 only when a library holds a stated `Unknown` row or a step (otherwise 1, or 2 for left-hand taps, as before). An `Unknown` row that only repeats the tool's own rpm/feed is not written, so plain tools save byte for byte as before (MCP `get_job` output unchanged for them).
- **Tool page.** The "Cutting data by material" group is now a table: Material, Spindle rpm, Feed, Stepdown, Stepover (0 = not stated). The `Unknown` row is first, its material fixed, not removable.
- **Behaviour change, inside a command only:** stating a document material the tool has no row for now runs the tool's `Unknown` row (before: the previous material's numbers stayed). An operation's milling feed still moves only for a row that names the material (#890's rule), so picking a material never overwrites hand-set op feeds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2015-unknown-cutting-row.md` (why `Option<WorkMaterial>` and not a `WorkMaterial::Unknown` variant: `WorkMaterial::row()` indexes the handbook table).

Base: upstream/main (`31f8d03d7`); no file overlap with #2029 (it does not touch `tool_cutting_rows.rs`; both touch `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in different places). Fork synced at the current upstream main for this branch.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/tools/tests/unknown_row.rs` (6): selection order, step fallback, derivation once and only from the running numbers, kinds that get none, refusals (bad steps, `Unknown` twice).
- `crates/app/tests/cutting_unknown_row.rs` (9): `a_new_tool_gets_its_unknown_row_from_its_own_numbers`, `a_v62_project_loads_its_tool_numbers_as_the_unknown_row_with_no_loss`, `a_v1_tool_library_loads_with_the_unknown_row_and_steps_write_v3`, `the_row_is_picked_by_the_stock_then_the_document_then_unknown`, `a_second_setup_stock_material_seeds_only_its_own_operations`, `steps_seed_only_in_commands_and_the_stock_material_round_trips`, `a_project_with_no_new_rows_posts_the_same_s_and_f_words` (posts, re-saves as v62, reloads, re-posts: identical S/F words), `a_stated_stepover_wider_than_the_cutter_is_refused_by_tool_name`, `mcp_sets_the_stock_material_as_one_undo_step`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_material.rs`: the stock page's Material group sits between Shape and Size, and a pick is one undoable `SetStockMaterial`.
- Updated to the new law: `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs` (stating plastics, which has no row, now runs the tool's Unknown row), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs` unit tests (Unknown is shown, never added).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, m5): green on 75031d5f9 (tools, app and ui suites; 6.2 min). Clippy on camcraft-tools, camcraft-app, camcraft-ui: clean (`--all-targets -D warnings`).

## UI before and after

These are headless captures of the real egui controls, rendered with `egui_kittest::Harness::render` on Linux. Before is pre-feature commit `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239`. After is reviewed head `af78aec60436e402c8e026d5bc9521552131bf5a`. The temporary harness called the shipping `cutting_rows` and `stock_page` functions; no UI was mocked. The cutting-data draft has the same Aluminium 6061 row in both captures. The after draft also states stepdown 2 mm and stepover 3 mm. The stock captures use the same seeded document.

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, at commit `b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d`. No capture harness, screenshot, golden, or review evidence was added to this PR branch.

| Control | Before | After |

| Cutting data | ![Cutting data before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-before.png) | ![Cutting data after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-after.png) |

The after table shows the fixed Unknown row, the named material row, and the step fields. The after stock page shows the Material group between Shape and Size. Both render checks passed at each revision (four captures total). This was a headless UI render, not a manual native-window session.

## Not exercised

Changelog: Tools keep cutting data per work material with an Unknown default row, an optional stepdown and stepover per row, and a setup stock may state its own material, which picks the row (stock, then document, then Unknown); older projects and tool libraries load unchanged (#2015)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: feat(motion): cut the adaptive stock ring from the air (issue 1950, rounds A-B)
body:
﻿Draft. Rounds A to E of issue #1950 (a default whole-model Adaptive 3D Pocket exceeds the planner budgets on the stock ring). This PR does not close the issue: the D plate level still goes to the Offset rings, now by the hop budget. Round F is open.

Head: c3509172c331eedacbf61f8a07855cadd12fdb75

## What changed

Round A (motion crate):
- New planner `plan_from_air` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs`. It cuts the stock ring from the air side inward. Sources: Held 1991 (LNCS 500), Held and Spielberger 2009 (CAD 41(7)), Stori and Wright 2000.
- `Raster::open_air` marks the air band as open. The walk functions of `raster.rs` moved to `raster/walk.rs` with no change of logic.

Round B (plumbing, no new algorithm):
- `machining3d::open_sides` takes a `stock_band` argument. `machining3d::stock_band(r, adaptive)` gives `2r + OPEN_SLACK` for Adaptive and `r - OPEN_SLACK` for each other strategy.
- New entry `machining3d::pocket3d_open_prev(facets, footprint, stock, p, mask)`. The stock goes through `ladder`, `hsm::plan_level`, `adaptive_passes` and `hsm_passes`.
- A plan from the air whose worst reading is over the load bound is refused by name. The level then goes to the Offset rings with a note.

Round C:
- App arm (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `open_side.rs`): a whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy (not shell, not rest roughing) uses the wide band and calls `pocket3d_open_prev` with the setup stock outline. Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and each other strategy keep the old band.
- Microlift joins (`adaptive/air_links.rs`): each pass is joined to the one before it by the existing `LinkLaw`. Each join is walked again on the stock. A pass with no proved join keeps its retract hop. Source: Otkur and Lazoglu 2007.

Round D:
- Air entry: `machining2d::in_air(stock, e, r)`. Where the first pass of an air plan starts 0.005 mm clear of the stock outline, the ladder enters the level by an axial plunge there. A tool that is not centre-cutting keeps the old entry law.
- Fixture refusal: `air_band_refusal` refuses the Adaptive whole-model op at generation when a tagged fixture meets the air band. The message starts with `AIR_BAND_FIXTURE` and names the fixture. The post gate is not changed.

Round E:
- Cause of the round D crossing at (-8.12, -35.61). A probe printed the crossing pairs of the air passes before and after the joins. Before the joins: 40 pairs. After the joins: the same 40 pairs. So the joins and the air entry did not cause it. Pass 0 is the spiral (3 closed fronts and a closing lap on ring 3 at y -35.607). Passes 1-21 are open-front runs. Passes 22-45 are wall laps. The pairs were:
  - the spiral and the first open runs: a lead-in starts one load width back, on the ring 3 lap, and steps past it;
  - each open run and the run of the next front (1-4, 4-7, ...);
  - open runs and wall laps (4-37, 7-22, ...): a run that meets the part wall cuts across the laps.
- Fix, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_uncross.rs` (new): each new pass drops the chords that cross a kept pass, by the plan's own law (`guard::crosses`). The pass then continues as a new piece. Each piece is read on the stock as before, so the rest and the load readings stay true. Result: 0 crossing pairs before the joins.
- The joins: with the bare passes clean, `LinkLaw::late` (a lead whose graze joins the pass) put crossings back, because the lead runs back across an earlier pass. `air_joins` now keeps a late join only when the grown pass crosses no other pass. If it crosses, the join falls back to the retract hop. Result: 0 crossing pairs after the joins.
- The crossing check, the load check, the verify gate and the budgets are not changed.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs` (427 lines) is split. The landing spots (wall margin, spots along the first pass, the helix placement, the plunge spot) move to `machining3d/descent_place.rs` (120 lines) with no change of logic. `descent.rs` is now 327 lines.

## Readings, round E (D plate, R = 5, 70 x 70 stock, one level, debug)

| Reading | Round C/D (crossing plan) | Round E |
|---|---|---|
| Crossing through `adaptive_passes` | at (-8.12, -35.61) | none |
| Passes | 47 | 61 |
| Retract hops (budget 8) | 3 | 23 |
| Worst load (of D) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) |
| Slack to the bound | 0.00135 deg | 0.00135 deg |
| Moves (budget 120000) | 17614 | 17549 |
| Cut / air / lift (mm) | - / - / 107.3 | 2632 / 338 / 108 |
| Rest (limit 0.02) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| Time, one level (debug) | 21.8 s | 22.0 s |
| Strategy of the level | Offset rings (crossing) | Offset rings (hop budget) |

22 of the 23 hops are late joins that were refused because their lead crosses an earlier pass. The earlier reading of 3 hops came from joins whose leads crossed. The hop budget was not raised.

## Posted G-code

- Changed. Each whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy and a stock outline uses the wide band. A level whose air plan is clean and in its budgets is cut from the air. Other levels go to the Offset rings by name, as before.
- On the D plate, the stock ring level is still cut by the Offset rings (by name, now for the hop budget).
- Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and the non-Adaptive strategies post as before.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::adaptive::air_uncross::tests::a_crossing_chord_is_dropped_and_the_pass_goes_on` (new).
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`: still red, now on the hop budget (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason.
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`: red on its hop assert (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason. Its rest and move asserts hold.
- `no_stock_keeps_the_growth_spiral`, `an_air_plan_over_the_load_bound_is_refused_by_name`: pass.
- `pocket3d_air_band`: 4 pass.

Round E runs:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib -- ring_tests air_rings air_uncross machining3d pocket adaptive`: 87 pass, 0 fail, 9 ignored (built before the descent split; the split is a move only, and clippy built it clean).
- App: `level_links` 25, `open_band` 7, `operations` 120 / 6 ignored, `pocket3d_air_band` 4, `pocket3d_hsm` 1 / 2 ignored, `pocket3d_open_side` 7, `whole_model_pocket` 5 / 1 ignored. All pass (after the split).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: fix(fidelity): a stock copy of an incomplete model keeps naming its hole
body:
A stock copied from an incomplete model (#1610) now keeps naming that model's hole after the model is deleted. Before this change, its refusal at the post fell back to "saved before CamCraft recorded mesh fidelity (project v58 or older)". The post still refused it; only the reason given was wrong.

Fixes #1700

## What changed

The copy's refusal read the hole from the source model by name (`mesh_open::unknown_note`), so once the source was gone the lookup found nothing. Now the copy carries the hole itself (`schema::MeshOpen`), beside the fidelity-unknown sentinel it already carried (#1056):

- **Where the hole is copied:** every place that lands the sentinel on a copy now lands the hole with it:
  - `SetStock` and its undo
  - a setup clone (`CreateSetup` with a datum)
  - an undone `DeleteSetup`
  - `UpdateModel`'s refresh of the copies, and its undo
  - the project loader
- **Where the refusal reads it:** `model_fidelity::op_problem` reads the hole off the entity that carries the sentinel. Two small helpers: `mesh_open::hole_behind` (the twin of `model_fidelity::chord_behind`) and `mesh_open::note_for`.
- **Project file:** the saver already wrote `mesh_open` for any entity that has one. The loader now also accepts it on a `FromModel` stock marked `fidelity_unknown`, and a hole without the mark stays corrupt. There is no version bump: #1610's check (a hole on anything but a model is corrupt) has not shipped in a cut yet, so no released reader refuses these files.

The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/1700-stock-copy-hole.md`.

## How tested

- **New:** `crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs` (6 tests). A copy carries the hole, and its refusal names the source and the hole:
  - after the source is deleted, and across undo and redo of that delete;
  - after save, load, and a second save that matches byte for byte;
  - through a setup clone and an undone setup delete;
  - through a whole re-import of the source (which clears it) and that re-import's undo;
  - through `SetStock`'s undo.

  The file also checks that a stock with a hole and no mark fails to load as corrupt.
- **Without the fix,** the two "source deleted" tests fail: the refusal reads "saved before CamCraft recorded …".
- **Existing tests:** the `import_step_open_shell` tests from #1610 still pass. Its corrupt-file message check passes too, because the new message keeps the old wording as a prefix.
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (112 app suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branched from upstream/main after #1699 merged, not from a cut tag: the code this fixes is not in v0.20.0.

title: fix(ui): keep the near plane and the ortho eye consistent with the zoom
body:
### Summary

A viewport fix for the way the camera eats the model from the inside.

Two ways the camera clipped the model while zooming:

- **Perspective:** the near plane was a fixed 0.1 mm from the eye, so at close zoom the geometry right in front of the near plane clipped instead of rendering — zooming in went through the model. The near plane now rides `dist` (0.1 % of the view depth, clamped to 1e-5 min and 0.1 max).
- **Orthographic:** `dist` moved the eye, so zooming dollied the eye into the model and clipped through its faces from inside. The eye now sits at a fixed nominal distance (100 mm) behind the target, and `dist` is only a zoom factor for the view box's half-height — the way it was always meant to work. The near plane now reaches far behind the eye plane: `-((dist * 20.0).max(1000.0) - ORTHO_EYE_DIST)`.

Changelog: UI — the perspective near plane moves with the dolly distance and the orthographic camera's near plane no longer clips through geometry while zooming.

The tests pin the new ortho depth formula and a point in front of the eye plane (`dist = 300`, 150 mm back from the target), asserting it stays inside the clip volume.

### Verification

`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` — 803 passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets` — clean. No posted G-code, collision check, stock simulation math or geometry changed.

No issue covers this viewport bug yet — a maintainer will file one.

- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A new bar button (a four-armed cross, after Pick through) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default. It is view state like Pick through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the bounding-box centre of the part. Each arm ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at all zoom levels. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** A press on a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. A press on empty space still orbits. When a nav tool of the bar (Orbit, Pan, Zoom) is latched, that tool owns the press. While the button is down, the preview moves the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it with an offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows above the bar. The distance is the point where the cursor ray is nearest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the `MoveModel::new` of the Model page, with the rotation copied bit for bit. Thus a drag is one undo step, with the same staleness, the same following stock and the same fixture-clash warning as a typed move. There is no new placement path.

No new app command, thus no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`. The MCP `move_model` tool (`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs`) already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make each move that a drag makes.

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
The stack parents #517 (#417) and #518 (#418) are merged. The diff now holds only the #419 work.

## Merge-time refresh (maintainer's session, head 39632f647)
The maintainer's session took this PR over for a merge-time refresh. It merged `origin/main` (62e1d36a6) into the branch. It did not rebase or force-push.

Hand-resolved hunks (keep both sides):
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `threadHalfTurn`: the PR's dip chain is kept. Main changed the lead word from `fr()` to `fl()` (#902: an inch lead has six decimals). Both G32 blocks of the chain (the plain block and the dip block `G32 X Z F`) now use `fl()`. The three refusals of the chain (no open chain, steeper than 45 degrees, deeper than the pass) are kept.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, manifest: `continuousThreading = true` with its citation, and main's `workOffsetIndex`, `workOffsetMax`, `explainWords`, `explainTool`, `programUnits`, `explains`, `commentMax`, `explainBlockMax`.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, G76 header comment: the PR's chip-break dips clause and main's `g76Allowance` paragraph (#517). `g76Why` keeps the two refusals: `RepeatEachDepth` (#518) and `ChipBreakDips`.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: main's manifest list with `continuousThreading` added ("the last nine").
- `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`: the `ChipBreakDips` refusal and main's `MillSpindle` reverse refusal (#988).
- `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`: the `continuous_threading` and `mill_spindle_reverse` fields.

No refusal of #517, #518 or main is lost. The Tormach lathe post does not declare `continuousThreading`, so the engine refuses dips on it by name. Its G76 `RepeatEachDepth` refusal (#518) is unchanged. `git diff origin/main --stat` lists only the 26 files of this PR.

Readings after the refresh (`cargo test -j 6 -p <crate> --test <binary>`, one binary at a time):
- camcraft-motion: `turning_thread_dips` 9/9, `turning_thread_cycle` 3/3, `turning_thread_infeed` 10/10, lib 366 passed (5 ignored).
- camcraft-post: `inverted_post` 16/16, `recorded_streams` 12/12, lib 54/54.
- camcraft-cl: lib 41/41.
- camcraft-app: `lathe_post_thread_dips` 6/6 (golden `thread_g32_dips.nc` unchanged), `lathe_post_g76` 8/8, `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 7/7, `lathe_post_tormach_thread` 8/8, `lathe_post_css` 10/10, `turning_thread` 10/10, `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5, `lathe_thread_travel` 2/2, `conformance` 7/7, `coarse_laws` 6/6, `lathe_field_tools` 2/2, `project_roundtrip` 73/73.
- camcraft-ui: lib filter `thread` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised by the refresh: an inch program with dips (the `fl()` lead word under G20 has no golden), and a run on a controller or a simulator.

MCP: the dips ride the generic `edit_operation` tool through the project params JSON (`ThreadInfeedDto.dips`). No new MCP tool is necessary.

Screenshots: before and after screenshots on the refreshed head are in the section "Screenshots (Passes tab)" below.

Note: `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs` (600 lines) and `js.rs` (529 lines) were already more than 400 lines on main. This PR adds 4 and 17 lines to them.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

Changelog: Threading: optional in-pass chip-break dips on roughing passes, posted as continuous G32 X Z F segments by the Fanuc lathe post (#419)

Fixes #419

## Screenshots (Passes tab)

Headless render (egui_kittest Harness::render()) of the Threading Passes tab, on the refreshed head 39632f647. Before is origin/main. The page header still reads "Contour1": the harness retypes the draft of the seeded operation, not the operation itself. Dip height and Dip length show only when Chip-break every is not 0. The after image uses Chip-break every 3.0 mm, Dip height 0.2 mm and Dip length 1.0 mm.

Before (origin/main): the Passes tab ends with Repeat each depth and Hand. No dip rows.

![before](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/65e120d963438e7a2bbc1873e623da182637a2c4/pr-468/before.png?raw=true)

After (this PR): the rows Chip-break every, Dip height and Dip length sit between Repeat each depth and Hand.

![after](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/65e120d963438e7a2bbc1873e623da182637a2c4/pr-468/after.png?raw=true)
